description: The SHARING clause / OPEN SHARING phrase (ISO 12.4.5.15 / 14.9.27) - governs whether another file connector may open the same physical file (Table 19 -> status 61). A COBOL-2002 introduction; {is2002()}?-gated, so below 2002 the W1.5 parse-layer mapping names the edition (0900). THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the ANSI X3.23-1985 sequential file control entry ends `[ ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL ] [ FILE STATUS IS data-name-2 ] .` (§1985:VII.2.3.2) and its OPEN is `OPEN { INPUT file-name-1 [ REVERSED | WITH NO REWIND ] … | OUTPUT { file-name-2 [ WITH NO REWIND ] } … | I-O { file-name-3 } … | EXTEND { file-name-4 } … } …` (§1985:VII.4.3.2), with no sharing phrase in either; §2002:12.3.4.15 introduces the clause: 'The SHARING clause indicates that a file is to participate in file sharing and record locking', §2002:14.8.26.3 GR22 the OPEN phrase: 'The SHARING phrase overrides any SHARING clause in the file control entry of file-name-1', and §2002:F.2 states the change, its item 52: 'File sharing provides a cooperative environment that allows the user to permit or deny access by concurrent file connectors to a physical file.' §2014:12.4.4.14 and §2014:14.9.26.3 GR22 carry the 2002 text unchanged, so 2014 = 2023 (VCR row 7.39 records the facility's behavior at 85).
display: the SHARING clause / OPEN SHARING phrase
source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. ROWSH.
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
       FILE-CONTROL.
           SELECT F ASSIGN TO "f.dat" ORGANIZATION IS SEQUENTIAL
               SHARING WITH ALL OTHER LOCK MODE IS MANUAL.
       DATA DIVISION.
       FILE SECTION.
       FD F.
       01 R PIC X(8).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN. STOP RUN.
